full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the defendant-petitioner calls in question the orders dated 6-10-96 and 9-10-96 passed by the Assistant Judge, Kochua, Chandpur in Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 1996 allowing restoration of Title Suit No. 109 of 1995 to its original file and number by setting aside the order dated 17-6-96 dismissing the said suit for default. 

 5. The plaintiff-opposite party thereafter filed Miscellaneous. Case No. 16 of 1996 under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the suit by setting aside the order of dismissal. 

 6. The defendant-petitioner contested the said Miscellaneous. Case by filing written objection contending that the plaintiff-opposite party took 17 (seventeen) adjournments in a row in order to avoid trial and harass the defendant-petitioner and, as such, the suit should not be restored by setting aside the order of dismissal. 

 8. I have perused the impugned orders and considered the lower court records. In this case the plaintiff-opposite party took as many as 17 adjournments in a row since the first date of hearing until 17-6-96 mostly on the ground of non- attendance of witnesses or absence of his lawyer. From the nature of grounds of adjournments, it appears that the plaintiff-opposite party has filed a frivolous suit and, as such, he is trying to avoid the trial by raising false pleas thereby causing serious prejudice and untold sufferings to the defendant- petitioner. The plaintiff-opposite party's conduct amounts to a deliberate abuse of the Court's process by taking adjournments of hearing on false grounds. 

 10. The trial Court, having allowed the aforesaid 17 adjournments of hearing in a row has not only committed an error of law occasioning miscarriage of justice but also contributed to the abuse of the court process committed by the plaintiff-opposite party. This apart, the failure on the part of the plaintiff-opposite party to conduct the hearing of the suit on 17-6-96, if considered in the context of his past conduct, cannot be said to be due to any sufficient cause as contemplated under Order 9, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
